sentence_stem: Feeling tired after the long walk,
correct_completion: Tom sat down on the bench.
full_sentence: Feeling tired after the long walk, Tom sat down on the bench.
acceptable_variants: Tom sank onto the bench to rest.
Tom found a bench and rested on it.

options.text: the long walk sat down on the bench.
options.why_wrong: A walk cannot feel tired or sit down. In a participle clause, the subject of the main clause must be the person who does the action in the participle phrase.

options.text: Tom will sit down on the bench tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future time 'tomorrow' does not match 'feeling', which describes the same moment as the main action.

options.text: Tom sat down on the bench.
Tom sits down on the bench every day.
options.why_wrong: The habitual present describes a routine, while the participle clause describes a single event in the past.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with a shared subject
explanation: The participle clause 'Feeling tired after the long walk' must describe the subject of the main clause. Only Tom can feel tired, so only the option with Tom as the subject fits. Polish speakers often prefer a full subordinate clause with 'because' or 'when' here, but English participle clauses are shorter and must share the subject of the main clause.
translation: Czując się zmęczony po długim spacerze, Tom usiadł na ławce.
